stories.title: Passivhaus projects quadruple in Australia
stories.summary: Certified Passivhaus projects in Australia have grown from 48 at the end of 2022 to 201 by October 2026. More than 40 of these buildings will open for public tours in November. The standard is now applied to homes, schools, offices and community facilities across the country.

stories.title: Architects lobby for national retrofit programme
stories.summary: A coalition of 23 built environment organisations is urging the UK government to commit to a long-term national retrofit programme as COP31 begins in Turkey. The group, led by RIBA, wants stronger support for delivery and international collaboration on whole-life carbon. The government has yet to respond.

stories.title: EmiratesGBC hosts 14th MENA Green Building Awards
stories.summary: Emirates Green Building Council held its 14th annual awards ceremony in Dubai to honor regional sustainability achievements. The event was organized in partnership with various national green building councils across the Middle East and North Africa and endorsed by the World Green Building Council.

stories.title: India eyes $22.7 trillion net-zero investment
stories.summary: A new report suggests India's 2070 net-zero transition could unlock $22.7 trillion in investment opportunities across renewable energy, grids and green hydrogen. The study notes that while domestic resources may cover 70 percent of requirements, international capital remains essential to bridge the remaining $6.5 trillion financing gap.

stories.title: India’s Net-Zero Goal Opens $22.7 Trillion Investment Opportunity by 2070 - India Business Trade
stories.summary: A new report by Australian economist Nicki Hutley highlights massive investment opportunities in renewable energy, electricity grids, battery storage and green hydrogen as India pursues its 2070 net-zero target. Highlights - India’s net-zero transition could require $22.7 trillion in investment by 2070. - The country

stories.title: USGBC launches indoor air quality hub for schools
stories.summary: The U.S. Green Building Council has introduced a resource hub to help schools address indoor air quality. The initiative provides guidance on managing mold, wildfire smoke and HVAC issues. The organization notes that air quality can affect student health, comfort and attendance in school buildings.

stories.title: Porsche Design Tower Bangkok receives LEED Gold precertification
stories.summary: The 22-residence Porsche Design Tower Bangkok has achieved LEED Gold precertification. The design-stage review confirms the project is on track for full certification upon its scheduled completion in December 2028. The development aims to address energy efficiency, resource use and indoor environmental quality.

stories.title: Odisha signs transport planning deal with SPA Bhopal
stories.summary: The Odisha State Transport Authority has signed a memorandum of understanding with the School of Planning and Architecture in Bhopal. The partnership aims to create an integrated vision document for the state's transport infrastructure, covering water, rail, air, passenger and goods movement through 2036.

stories.title: NSE unveils design for new Mumbai headquarters
stories.summary: The National Stock Exchange has revealed the architectural design for its new headquarters in Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex. Designed by Hafeez Contractor, the building will occupy approximately 10,995 square metres on land leased from the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority for 80 years. Construction is now underway.

stories.title: Powerhouse Parramatta opens in Western Sydney
stories.summary: Powerhouse Parramatta opens this week, featuring a dramatic exoskeleton designed by Moreau Kusunoki and Genton. The project serves as a second venue for the 150-year-old museum of applied arts and sciences, situated on the banks of the Parramatta River near the city's second central business district.

stories.title: Design Doha returns to Qatar
stories.summary: The second edition of Design Doha has launched in the historic Fereej Al Asmakh neighbourhood. The expanded event features over 20 exhibitions and more than 300 multidisciplinary designers. The programme includes five public commissions focused on regional approaches to water, materials, craft, climate and the built environment.

stories.title: Mamdani architecture exhibition details unavailable
stories.summary: Information regarding the architecture exhibition mentioned in the Domus Web report is currently inaccessible. The server returned an access denied error for the requested page. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Finchley Road apartment towers mimic stone formations
stories.summary: Architect Amin Taha has completed a residential project on London’s Finchley Road featuring towers of pink basalt and igneous larvikite. The design aims to create an unmissable landmark above the railway station, described by the architect as a multistorey Stonehenge for commuters struggling to find the entrance.

stories.title: Viking legend inspires Icelandic mountain viewpoint
stories.summary: Arkibygg Architects and Esja Architecture have completed the Ring of Bjólfur in Seyðisfjörður. The viewpoint is designed to resemble a giant silver ring left on the burial site of a legendary Viking settler. It provides improved access to a ridge overlooking the town and surrounding peaks.

stories.title: ZAV Architects adds colourful extension to Tehran home
stories.summary: ZAV Architects has completed Golmorad, an extension to a villa in Kouhsar featuring overlapping arches that shift from terracotta to blue. The project expands the original weekend home into a permanent residence by incorporating three adjacent orchard plots into the structure's footprint.

stories.title: Germane Barnes to curate U.S. Pavilion at 2027 Venice Biennale
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department has selected the University of Miami School of Architecture to commission the U.S. Pavilion for the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale. Lead curator Germane Barnes will present an exhibition titled Earth Craft, exploring the relationship between American architecture and materials such as rammed earth.

stories.title: Scalpers headquarters completed near Seville
stories.summary: Estudio Hábito has completed the new 4,500 square metre headquarters for Scalpers near the site of Seville's Expo 92. The architects describe the building as a contemporary reinterpretation of Andalusian architectural tradition, utilising materials including brick and graphene-based coatings.

stories.title: Tatiana Bilbao designs for the passage of time
stories.summary: Architect Tatiana Bilbao rejects the industry standard of using materials that resist wear and weather. Instead, she designs buildings that welcome moss, leaves and encroaching roots. Her philosophy suggests that the most enduring architecture is that which eventually outgrows the architect's original intentions.

stories.title: CO2-cured concrete study shows strength gains
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a geopolymer concrete mixture using fly ash and GGBS that reached 68.4 MPa after 56 days. The study, published in Scientific Reports, suggests that combining CO2 curing with machine learning could improve strength. The paper remains unedited and is not yet considered established information.

stories.title: Aectual scales 3D printing production globally
stories.summary: Amsterdam-based Aectual is using Caracol’s Heron AM robotic network to 3D print circular building products. By utilising a distributed manufacturing model, the company aims to keep production close to clients worldwide. The first components are currently in production.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh begins 3D printed housing pilot
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh has broken ground on a 177-house pilot project using 3D concrete printing. The initiative aims to address the speed requirements of India's rural housing programme, which targets 4.95 crore homes by 2029. Traditional construction remains the standard for the vast majority of these builds.

stories.title: Energy codes drive demand for insulated glass adhesives
stories.summary: A report by IndexBox indicates that the global market for adhesives and sealants used in insulated glass is entering 2026 with more disciplined procurement. The sector is increasingly shaped by energy efficiency requirements for windows and facades in residential and commercial buildings.

stories.title: Fairbanks Morse Defense ships 3D-printed submarine part
stories.summary: Fairbanks Morse Defense has shipped its first 3D-printed SUBSAFE Level 1 component, a copper-nickel tailpiece produced with Lincoln Electric. The company states the milestone is a significant step toward normalizing additive manufacturing for U.S. Navy submarine maintenance and sustainment.

stories.title: Birds incorporate human debris into nest designs
stories.summary: Recent observations show birds constructing nests from anti-bird spikes and 3D-printed scaffolds. These structures are being cited as examples of posthuman architecture, where discarded human materials and experimental debris are repurposed by species to create shared habitats.

stories.title: Northwestern researchers develop hybrid 3D printing method
stories.summary: Researchers at Northwestern University have created direct ink additive lithography, a hybrid 3D printing process. The method combines ink sheet extrusion with a moving projector to print functional, particle-filled fluids at higher speeds and resolutions than traditional light-based printers.

stories.title: Wave-shaped surfaces tested for hurricane wind protection
stories.summary: Researchers at the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering found that wave-shaped roof and wall geometries reduced peak wind pressures by up to 60 percent in laboratory tests. The team used 3D-printed structures in a wind tunnel to study how these shapes disrupt swirling air patterns.

stories.title: U.S. mass timber buildings increase significantly
stories.summary: The number of commercial and public mass timber buildings in the U.S. has grown to more than 1,500, up from fewer than 100 a decade ago. Timber growers are now targeting data-center developers as a housing slump impacts sawmill demand.

stories.title: Kashmir musk deer face steep habitat losses
stories.summary: A new study projects that climate change could reduce suitable habitat for the Kashmir musk deer by 82.6 percent by 2100 under high-emissions scenarios. Wildlife corridors may contract by half, increasing the risk of population isolation. The species is currently native to the western Himalaya.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh prepares net-zero roadmap for MSMEs
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh is developing a roadmap to help micro, small and medium enterprises transition toward net-zero emissions. The state is partnering with the Union Government and Energy Efficiency Services Limited to improve industrial energy efficiency and global competitiveness. The initiative follows national recognition of the state’s existing efforts.

stories.title: India targets 10 billion dollars in energy storage investment
stories.summary: India has approved a 1.5 billion dollar scheme to develop 92 GWh of grid-scale storage capacity by 2031. The government expects the initiative to attract 10 billion dollars in total investment. The plan includes 60 GWh of pumped hydro, 30 GWh of battery storage and 2 GWh of emerging technologies.

stories.title: SMP Kolkata expands role in urban transformation
stories.summary: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port is moving beyond traditional operations to focus on riverfront development, infrastructure and civic amenities in Kolkata and Howrah. The port authority describes the approach as a forward-looking effort to act as a catalyst for urban transformation and holistic development in the region.

stories.title: Nila Spaces develops wellness homes at GIFT City
stories.summary: Nila Spaces is building wellness-led homes at GIFT City on a plot acquired for 6,557 rupees per square foot. The developer describes the project as a wellness-focused residential development. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Indian architect wins global golf design award
stories.summary: Aashish Vaishnava has become the first Indian architect to win the Golf Course Designer of the Year at the World Golf Awards. He shares the 2026 title with English partner Jon Hunt. The award has been presented annually since 2015, and this is the first time an Indian has won.

stories.title: Palampur loses heritage buildings to modern construction
stories.summary: Palampur is replacing century-old colonial buildings with modern concrete structures, prompting concern from historians and residents. The historic Government Senior Secondary School, established by missionaries 103 years ago, is among the landmarks lost. The city is gradually shedding its architectural identity to make way for new construction.

stories.title: Agra air quality fluctuates after Diwali
stories.summary: Air quality in Agra deteriorated following Diwali, with sensors at two locations recording an Air Quality Index above 400. While local sensors indicated severe pollution, the Central Pollution Control Board reported a moderate city-wide average of 190. Sensors and official monitors are currently in disagreement.

stories.title: Morang municipality completes bridge project early
stories.summary: A bridge project in Ratuwamai Municipality was completed 10 months ahead of the contract schedule. The infrastructure, built at a cost of 6 crore 53 lakh rupees, features a 25-meter pile foundation with a carriageway and footpaths. Local residents are reportedly happy with the early delivery.

stories.title: Machine learning improves urban heat mapping
stories.summary: Researchers found that integrating localized architectural geometry into machine learning algorithms improves the mapping of urban microclimates. The study contrasted satellite imagery with three-dimensional urban form parameters in Indianapolis and Bloomington. The method aims to better identify heat disparities in small and mid-sized cities.

stories.title: Savannah residents provide flood data after FEMA models fail
stories.summary: Savannah is collecting data from residents to address chronic drainage problems after federal flood models failed to capture local conditions. The city is bypassing standard federal mapping to solve issues that residents have long reported. The models were apparently unaware of the water.

stories.title: Philadelphia expands public performance dashboards
stories.summary: Philadelphia has updated its public performance dashboard to include data on street sweeping and reports of unsafe properties. The city aims to provide transparency on municipal services. Residents can now track exactly what the city is doing, or failing to do, in real time.

stories.title: Illinois appeals FEMA disaster aid denial
stories.summary: Governor JB Pritzker is appealing the denial of federal disaster relief for August storms. The state updated its damage estimate to 43 million dollars, exceeding the 24.9 million dollar threshold required for assistance. FEMA previously denied the request without providing an explanation.

stories.title: Local agencies face integration hurdles for spatial AI
stories.summary: State and local agencies are struggling to integrate spatial AI due to a lack of uniform infrastructure across legacy and modern systems. Agencies must bridge data from diverse sensors and traffic controls. Building a digital twin is one proposed solution, though it comes with significant costs.

stories.title: Gdańsk launches competition for urban density project
stories.summary: The Gdańsk Social Housing Association is seeking urban planning concepts to increase density in a block near Plac Wałowy. The competition requires a mix of residential and commercial development on a 750-square-meter site. Submissions are due by 27 November 2026.

stories.title: Birmingham nightlife district sees mixed development
stories.summary: Birmingham’s Digbeth district is undergoing significant investment, including new studios, residential flats and a tram route. While some argue these changes threaten the area's nightlife, others suggest the infrastructure improvements are making the district more accessible. The tram route is currently waiting for tracks to be laid.

stories.title: Indian cities lack consideration for children
stories.summary: Indian urban planning is designed for adult convenience with little regard for children's safety or play. Exposure to pollution has led to high rates of respiratory issues among adolescents in cities like Delhi. The outdoors has become increasingly detrimental to the health of the city's youngest residents.

stories.title: Mashup Ventures closes 17.6 million dollar fund
stories.summary: Mashup Ventures has closed a 25.9 billion won fund to invest in artificial intelligence and deep tech startups. The fund was raised without government policy money and will focus on pre-seed and seed-stage companies. It has a 10-year lifespan.

stories.title: xFigura platform consolidates AI models for architects
stories.summary: The generative design platform xFigura aims to solve the friction of AI ethics and design agency by consolidating 90 AI models into a single canvas. Founded by architect George Guida, the platform positions itself as a production infrastructure for the design process. The appeal is obvious.

stories.title: Trimble adds AI capabilities to construction platform
stories.summary: Trimble has announced new AI capabilities for its Connect platform, aiming to turn industry risk into confidence across the design and build lifecycle. The tools include generative design and customer-designed agents. The company says the update closes operational gaps while preserving deep specialisation for project teams.

stories.title: Octave launches AI-enabled facilities management tool
stories.summary: Octave Intelligence has released Octave Attune Facilities, a cloud-based platform for managing multiple sites. The tool includes a built-in AI assistant for all SaaS subscriptions, allowing users to query operational data through natural-language questions. The platform combines maintenance data with mobile access and digital twin capabilities.

stories.title: Mavria raises $130 million for factory-built data centers
stories.summary: Mavria has raised $130 million at a $1 billion valuation to build standardized 5 MW data center units in a factory. While the startup targets frontier AI labs, it has not published capacity, pricing, or delivery timelines. For its target customers, the open question is power.

stories.title: Mavria raises $130 million for factory-built data centers
stories.summary: Mavria has raised $130 million to build standardized, factory-integrated data centers. The company is currently constructing its first demonstration unit in Houston. Customers are responsible for supplying their own GPU servers, while Mavria provides the physical infrastructure. The startup was founded by three former Department of Energy employees.

stories.title: MIT computing college adds seven faculty members
stories.summary: The MIT Schwarzman College of Computing has hired seven new faculty members for 2026. The group will focus on applying artificial intelligence to fields including quantum computing, environmental science, and macroeconomics. Dean Dan Huttenlocher noted the hires are leading advances in computing and its impact on society.

stories.title: Stuckeman School to host lecture on circular architecture
stories.summary: The Stuckeman School at Penn State will host Swiss studio Parabase for a lecture on November 18. Titled Slow Events, the talk will explore circular strategies and alternative perspectives on reuse. The firm aims to question conventional modes of construction through an economy of means and materials.

stories.title: NVB Architects details approach to special needs school design
stories.summary: NVB Architects has spent over 30 years working in the education sector, with a focus on schools for special educational needs and disabilities. The practice recently developed a farm school concept for the sector. The studio is based in a Grade I-listed chapel in Somerset.

stories.summary: A tribute to the country’s first education minister on his birth anniversary, he championed an education system that combined scientific and technological progress with religious and moral values MAULANA ABUL KALAM AZAD, India’s first education minister, advocated an education system that combined modern scientific knowledge

stories.title: JJ School of Art begins first PhD program
stories.summary: The JJ School of Art has launched its first-ever PhD batch, receiving 88 applications for 16 available seats. The program marks a new academic milestone for the institution. Further details regarding the curriculum were not immediately available due to technical issues with the school website.

stories.title: UCLA launches hub to address racial equity in foster care
stories.summary: UCLA has launched the Racial Equity Hub for Child Welfare Reform to address racial disproportionalities in the foster care system. The initiative aims to shrink the number of Black families involved with child welfare by connecting researchers and policymakers with community members who have lived experience.

stories.title: Whitko students visit Notre Dame for art and architecture tour
stories.summary: Advanced art students from Whitko High School recently visited the University of Notre Dame to study art history and campus architecture. At the Raclin Museum of Art, students analyzed historical works to discuss how artists use different styles and perspectives to communicate ideas about the world.

stories.title: UVA Arctic Design Group wins industry award
stories.summary: The Arctic Design Group at the University of Virginia has been recognized in the 2026 Next Practices Awards by ArchDaily. The group investigates how architecture and landscape planning can respond to changing realities in Arctic settlements. It is directed by Leena Cho and Matthew Jull.

research.summary: CERN scientists have finally found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it happens only once in roughly 10 billion decays, ending a search spanning more than 40 years. The breakthrough could help physicists uncover hidden particles and forces that lie beyond the reach of today's most.

research.summary: A century-old theory about the origins of life on Earth may be wrong. research.summary: Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall in 2026 as renewable energy and electric vehicles gain ground, but rising emissions from deforestation threaten to push total CO2 emissions to a new record.
